column4: points to quingdao workshop in china on remp for indian ocean; on remp development procedure; italy doesnt want external remp commission; asks whether ccz remp is underway; asks if ltc will engage with bbnj scientific body; wants sharing of data from test mining, promptly
column5: thank you, mr. president. italy would like to express its appreciation for the hard work and dedication of the legal and technical commission in drafting its report in such usual short time after the first part of the 30th session. we also wish to congratulate the newly re elected chair and vice chair. we thank them for their service, and are confident that their continued guidance will greatly benefit the work of the ltc. reference is made to the scientific workshop in qingdao, china, scheduled from 27 april to first of may 2025, on the development of the ramp for the indian ocean. italy is proud to have nominated one expert for the workshop, which confirms our active support for the timely development of such crucial element. and we look forward to significant results from the event in relation to the development of a standardized procedure for the development establishment and review of regional environmental management plans. italy acknowledged the significant effort involved in preparing such a comprehensive and thoughtful procedure, including the time dedicated during the intersessional period to get a comment and establish the methodology we recognize the importance of this standardized procedure in ensuring a rigorous, transparent and scientific, robust framework for managing the marine environment in the area, in line with the principles of cost effectiveness and in application of an evolutionary approach to environmental management. italy expresses reservations regarding the establishment of an additional independent committee for the remp process. we believe that the existing mechanism structures in place, including the resort to external expertise, are sufficient to address the scientific, technical and legal needs of the remp process and the introduction of further committees could potentially complicate and undermine the effectiveness of the overall system. furthermore, italy, respectfully, would like to inquire whether the ltc has commenced work on the review of the ccz environmental management ramp as part of the ongoing remp process. and what rob met the ltc intends to follow on a different topic, and following the publication of a report on the engagement of isa with the bbnj agreement, we look forward to hear from the ltc whether it intends to engage with the scientific and technical body under the bbnj framework to identify the area based management tools, including marine protected and related measures, we consider a priority that in this context, the authority retains its primacy in the selection of marine protected areas within the area. italy also welcomed the recent tax test conducted and acknowledged their valuable contribution to the scientific knowledge and data collection within the area. in this regard, italy kindly requests that the data collected from this test be shared promptly with the secret target to ensure full transparency and facilitate ongoing collaboration among all stakeholders involved. italy further welcomes the practice of holding side events during the second part of the council session by the ltc aimed at strengthening the cooperation between member states and stakeholders, this initiative is highly appreciated as it contributes to greater transparency and foster a constructive dialog among all relevant partners. italy remains committed to cooperating constructively with the framework of the commission and the authority, and look forward to further discussion on these important matters. thank you.

column4: wants external scientific expert mechanism; mentions data; wants webinars; contractors must share clear data; scientific rigor; thresholds comments; remps and independent experts; integration with databases; geological information should also be shared; environment and heritage important
column5: dear delegates, we are speaking on behalf of the african group. first and foremost, we would like to thank the ltc for its remarkable work over the first part of this 30 this session, the report presented reflects the breadth and the complexity of the tasks entrusted into it, but it also is forward looking. the african group would like to support this commitment to strengthen transparency through open meetings with external, independent experts, and in this sense, we encourage this mechanism to be institutionalized respecting confidentiality of essential data, and furthermore, we support parallel informal webinars for democratic engagements, and we've also closely taken note of the annual reports. it's imperative for the contractors to fully cooperate, giving clear data in respect of their contractual obligations. and the african group supports technical exchange in this regard on environmental impact, the china cmc cooperation and beijing high tech epc, they have been paid close attention to, and we underscore the importance of maintaining ongoing scientific rigor on biological impacts and the robustness of environmental monitoring this is important. looking towards the future, we also consider that the environmental impact must take place with scientific diligence. turning to environmental thresholds, we welcome content on toxicity and other topics mentioned in this report. we recommend that this be comprehensively added into the report and looking towards remps, we also support the proposal to giving remps clear legal value through the formal decision of the council. and furthermore, we have independent experts to support the scientific rigor of remps, and we believe that it's important for this to be shared regionally. there should be cooperation and financing with scientific bodies which should fully participate in this. we also need to improve the accessibility. and the african group encourages mobilizing additional resources to foster the integration into world databases, and we are also considering expansion of networks the african group believes that we should be actively engaged in this program in order to face the future, particularly in the case of the enterprise turning to contractual flexibility. we believe that, despite what is stated in the report, we need to make sure that the regulatory framework be complied with prospection is very, very important, and we need to bolster the dissemination of geological information. so to conclude, we are in favor of governments environmental responsibility and the protection of heritage. we will work with stakeholders to progress. thank you very much.

column4: nothing to add to morocco; notes french exploration contract (ifremer); wants contract extension (?); on member number of the cgt (ltc in french?); weak participation; time and money is an issue for participation
column5: merci monsieur, thank you, president, today i'd like to welcome everybody and say hello, and brilliant statement was just a digital and i have nothing to add to that, that was excellent. thank you very much for that president, dear colleagues. first of all, we would like to join our voices into what was said by italy. we would like to thank the head of the ltc for such a report, we also support the efforts of the commission working towards transparency, and also the comments about holding open meetings. we've had one in the past, and we encourage this type of meetings all of the members of the authorities and stakeholders can thus have information. and as morocco said, this transparency has been demonstrated. we also took note of the comments about the french contractor, and as head of the french delegation, i would like to join in in the second request in the report for restoring the contract as of 19, there was a major impact as of covid 19, that is, that has a major impact. we all know that the cgt is essential for the authority. it's an essential institution for the council. and if the council is a driver, the commission is its fuel, you could say it's highly refined, so it's extraordinarily important. over the years, well, we see that there's supposed to be 15 members according to the conventional convention, and it has been enlarged because we've had more and more work. there's more and more expertise here. and at the last meeting, we've renewed the cg ter, there are a lot of cg t, rather, there are a lot of groups in different geographical areas. now we have, i believe, 41 or 42 members, and this is why we are pretty concerned to see that for the first time, this is the first time that there's such a weak participation. we have the broadest, largest commission of all, but members are participating less. this is what we've seen over the course of these discussions. it was very difficult because of the composition of this cgt, so we need to give them the time to participate. and secondly, we need to be able to fund the missions and also have voluntary commission contributions to make that possible. thank you very much.

column4: aligns with morocco; happy to see training and knowledge transfer efforts; on participation; secretariat needs strengthening (ltc?); important for monitoring and inspecting contractors; thanks for the fund for participation

column4: commends thresholds work; definition of threshold values will be a big step in finding the balance between exploitation and protection; commends remp work; will accelerate the process of remp developing; important for starting mining; on uch and regional management tools; remps should form the basis of this; on eis and eia and test mining; ltc and contractor cooperation will help in data; deepdata and other databases; deepdate must be filled in with existing data not yet uploaded by contractors; important for deep sea research
column5: thank you for a possibility to speak mr. president. first and foremost, we would like to thank the members of the ltc for their work that was carried out in the intersessional period and during the first part of the 30th session on a large number of very important activities. we welcome the progress that has been achieved in the development of environmental thresholds with regard to key parameters, we agree with the need to further, further investigation of temporal and spatial parameters, the light pollution and noise pollution. also, we need to synchronize these environmental threshold, with other standards and guidelines and with the draft regulations, we expect that the ltc shall continue its work on this matter, and that the ltc shall draft a relevant report on it, we consider that the definition of threshold values for the admissible level of exploitation activity shall become a seminal step forward for to striking balance between the development of deep sea mineral resources, on the one hand and providing for effective protection of the marine environment on the other hand, we also welcome the development of the standardized procedure for the development, establishment and review of regional environmental management plans and the template of such plans. we think that the approval of this document by the council will give us a possibility to accelerate the process of developing regional environmental management plans for different regions where we have active contracts for the exploration of mineral resources. this is becoming even more important in the light of the currently draft regulations be development, and we understand that the concentration of an application for the approval of a plan of work is possible only and exclusively in the presence of a regional environmental management plan for this type of resource in a given region. we also note that the commentaries and proposals that had been discussed before with regard to the underwater cultural heritage and also also regional management tools and other matters are still valid. but having said that, we think that the proposed standardized procedure for the development establishment and review of regional environmental management plan is a very good basis for holding further discussions on these matters. with regard to the activities of the ltc, with regard to the eis and e i n done by the contractors, we think that the detailed analysis of these documents by the ltc and further joint work cooperation with the contractor on task test mining issues will give us a possibility to provide for their completeness, precision and statistical reliability. we also would like to note the significance of increasing the compatibility of the deep data, database of the authority with other active global databases. also it is important to populate this database by means of adding the data that had been acquired by the contractors in the earlier periods. we think that this type of data will be very useful for the evaluation of temporal and spatial variability of the environment, which is a necessary precondition for effective management in the region, and for further advancement of deep sea research. to conclude, once again, we would like to extend our gratitude to the chair of the ltc. we would like to thank for the for drafting of this detailed report. we underscore that a huge amount of work has already been done by the members of the legal and technical commission,

column4: happy with open meeting of ltc; notes low participation in commission; all members should contribute equally; notes remps; data in deepdata from scoping survey; recalls request from council on contractors who do not comply with data and report obligations; notes capacity building work; lists work that needs to be done before mining commences; s and g, remps and thresholds must be finalised before exploitation
column5: thank you, mr. president, and good morning to all portugal. thanks the chair of the legal and technical commission for preparing and presenting the report on the work of the commission at the first part of the 30th session of the council. let me start, mr. president by welcoming this comprehensive and detailed report, providing important details on the different aspects covered, like others before me, my delegation welcomes the open meeting of the ltc during last session of the council, and encourages the continuation of these good practices that significantly improve the transparency of the commission. we express our appreciation for the substantial work undertaken and share the concerns expressed by the chair, with the record low attendance of the members of the commission, putting an extra burden on the members that participated in this session, with the increasing complexity of the work that is asked from the ltc, it is crucial that all its members contribute equally to delivering its mandate. we commend the dedication of the attending members for their dedication, and extend our gratitude to the secretariat for its essential support in facilitating this work. we highlight the importance of ongoing work on developing key aspects of deep sea governance, namely the standards and guidelines, the environmental thresholds and the remps, ensuring that key regulatory instruments are in place before any mining activities can begin. it's absolutely priority. these instruments are critical to safeguarding the marine environment, providing clear parameters for industry operations and ensure that activities in the national sea bed area do not cause harmful effects to the marine environment. therefore, we encourage continuing progress in these areas and look forward to receiving further updates on their development in the upcoming sessions. we take note that the prospecting survey was analyzed by the commission and that it was concluded that it adhere to the rules, regulations and procedures for this activity. we welcome that the data collected was provided to the authority and it is available at the database. however, i recall the concerns expressed by delegation last year on the process for the timely communication of such activities to the commission and to the council, and would welcome further clarification on the procedure. to that end, we take note of the review of contractors annual reports and encourage continued efforts to ensure timely and comprehensive submissions. we also take note of the periodic review of the status of contracts for exploration and of the implementation of the plans of work. for plans of work, these reviews are a key mechanism for evaluating contractors performance, which is essential for maintaining transparency and accountability. we recall the requests by this council to have further information on the contracts that have not fulfilled their obligations and are susceptible of being in breach of their contracts. this information is the basis for monitoring and assessing responsibility of contractors, and if that cannot be done at the exploration phase, how can the council trust that it would be possible at the exploitation phase? we would forward, we look forward for the update on the reviews currently underway, and urge the commission to report to respond to the request of the council on further detailed information on the non compliant contractors. we also take note of the assessment of the environment impact statements for proposed text mining activities, and welcome the detailed information provided these review process is crucial, and we look forward to further updates on how environmental risks are being addressed. capacity building initiatives, particularly training programs for developing states, is essential for ensuring inclusive participation in cbd activities, and we support ongoing efforts to enhance knowledge transfer and technical expertise. looking ahead, we anticipate receiving further information in the upcoming reports, particularly on the outcomes of environmental impact assessments and effectiveness of monitoring measures, progress in developing standards and guidelines, with a focus on the required before any mining activity can commence, the establishment of environmental thresholds and the finalization of remps as critical safe guards, finding findings from ongoing, periodic reviews of contractors and enemies, necessary follow up actions and further updates on relinquishment requests and their implications for the sustainable use of cbd resources. more broadly, we emphasize that the development of standards and guidelines remains a priority, particularly those that must be in place before any mining activity can commence. likewise, the finalization of environmental thresholds and remps, it's a fundamental prerequisite for such activities. these regulatory and environmental safeguards are essential for the responsible management of deep sea resources, ensuring that activities in the area are carried out in accordance with the highest environmental and legal standards. once again, portugal, thanks the members of the legal and technical commission for their dedication and the secretary for its invaluable support in facilitating its work. i thank you, mr. president.

column4: commends ltc work; working pro bono; points out that ltc is a subsidiary (of the council?); notes time and financial constraints; not clear who werent able to attend; if developing countries can not attend, then that is a great problem; on non-comliance; isba/28/c/28 need to renew pressure so that ltc publicly name contractors that do not fulfill their obligations; isba/29/ltc/5; wants stronger repercussions; fourth year in a row that public naming has been called for; important to know about non-compliance when deciding on extending contracts; council might unknowingly extend non-compliant contractors contracts, who knows there are no repercussions; wants to know procedure behind not naming contractors, hard to believe this was consensus; supports extending india and france contracts; thresholds are the key to the whole mining regimes; wants threshold consultations publicly and in writing
column5: thank you very much, president. and good day to everyone. my legation would like to thank the ltc for their tenacious work.  we have instilled in them as a subsidiary subsidiary body, but such important recommendations reflect our trust in them, and costa rica wants to make its appreciation manifest. they're experts who work pro bono, leaving their other obligations aside for a while so that they can come and be our technical and legal advisors. so our appreciation is expressed hand in hand with a concern about the lack of participation of some members, and we're concerned because we understand the limitations that some of them may have, time constraints and even financial constraints. we're not certain who was unable to attend, but we are wondering whether or not it might have to do with a lack of funding in the trust fund for participation of representatives from developing countries, if with this were the case, we're very concerned that we're taking decisions where the developing countries are less represented. this was a great debate that had been underway for years, and we finally had a geographical balance struck within the ltc. but if the participation of everyone is not fostered, then really the job isn't fully done, or the purpose isn't fully accomplished. so all delegations that have it within their power to support the participation fund from developing countries, representatives from developing countries, both in the council and in the ltc, i would call upon them to do so. i would like to focus a bit more on an issue that is of concern to costa rica, and that is non compliance contractors, non compliance in decision isba stroke 28 strike sea strike 28 we believe that we need to renew our pressure so that the ltc appoints annually rather names those contractors who have not responded to the council's request to address issues of interest that were identified by the commission vis a vis their contractual obligations. this was very clear, because for at least four years, we've been requesting this section 10 of the ltc reports indicates that there was a response by the eight contractors that had been identified in the previous meeting, and although there were certain contractors that gave satisfactory information, others still owed further clarifications. and these eight contrast, contractors had already been at risk of non compliance in the previous session when we also requested the names of these contractors, paragraph 11 of the ltc report says that the contractors will be invited through the secretariat and following the adopted modalities to a virtual exchange reviews with the commission in may, costa rica believes that this is a bit unclear, because it seems that this is going to be addressed through a virtual exchange instead of applying the criteria that they adopted via the council, there are criteria to identify those who responded in completely, and we're referring to document isba 29 ltc five, and we should be naming these contractors to the secretary general and informing of this to the council. now this is of great concern to us, because this is the fourth year we're asking this. first we were told that we didn't have the ways and means to name them, and it seems there's still a reluctance to name those who are not complying. now, dear colleagues, we need to know which contractors are not complying, because as soon as there is a request for extension of their contract, and there's an application at least. costa rica believes that it's important to know whether those who are requesting an extension are not complying. we believe this is an important piece of information to put on the table when we decide on these extensions, we might unknowingly authorize or extend contractors who might understand that there are no consequences for them to non compliance. so we'll reiterate once again to the council that we believe that this is in sufficient and we truly need to take this seriously and name, without further ado, these contractors who have had many opportunities to correct themselves. we would also like to know what the procedure was to arrive at this decision, whether there was consensus or not, because it does seem that it's strange for all ltc members to agree not to follow with what the council had requested, turning to relinquishment that's deferred. we believe it's reasonable for france and india's requests to be met with. they both provided explanations. they were both affected by the covid period and other circumstances. so it seems that this deferred authorization vis a vis relinquishment is substantiated. costa rica would like to thank the work that is working on the thresholds for their work. the importance of thresholds is immense. in fact, the entire exploration regime depends on thresholds being clearly set, and they're being applicable science based and applying the precautionary principle. these are the thresholds that will determine whether a contract is awarded, they will be the most important measure in order to effectively protect the seabed. and this ties into responsible mining in the area. this is why the consultation to the stakeholders may mentioned rather in paragraph 24 is so crucial, we hope that the consultation will be done through a political procedure in writing. we haven't seen this yet, and we think it is very important for there to be uniform policies. isa, visa, stakeholders. we want this to be accessible, inclusive and transparent. we also see a role for each one of the isa member states so that they can have their own national consultations on these very important instruments, in order to be able to contribute their own views and experiences. costa rica also appreciates this open meeting that the ltc had was an open event, we hope to be able to participate in other such events. we understand there are certain issues that are confidential, but when there is no confidentiality at stake, it's important for states to know what's happening, and we believe that it would be the right thing to have open sessions once in a while, even more often than once in a while, if possible, in order to keep abreast of what's being decided in the ltc. thank you very much.

column4: notes low participation in commission; has donated 30 000 euros to be split between finance committee, council, and ltc, voluntary trust fund; wants names of non-compliant contractors published; isba/29/ltc/5 on non-compliance; isba/29/c/24 on council asking for names; thresholds, commends work of commission and wg; wg thresholds focus on polymetallic nodules; netherlands reiterates that thresholds should be developed for other resources as well; wg will work on identifying scientific needs; on remps; two debates ongoing about remps; one on procedure for developing; the other on the outcome of that procedure; wants similar process for remps as in thresholds; ltc supported by external experts
column5: thank you, mr. president. good morning, colleagues. first of all, let me thank the commission for its report. we express our sincere appreciation to the chair, vice chair, and all members of the commission for their hard work and dedication. we commend the commission for the points raised in its report, bringing to the attention of the council matters which indeed require consideration by the council. we note with concern, like others, however, the low attendance of members to this year's meeting, we consider it of the utmost importance that nominated members of the commission are provided with time and resources to carry out their work to enable the commission to play its important role in the institutional structure of the authority. in accordance with the convention, the kingdom of the netherlands has responded to the call from the council for contribution to the voluntary trust funds to support in the meetings of the authority by developing states, including in the council, the commission and the finance committee, we have recently contributed 30,000 euros to be divided equally between the voluntary trust fund for the council and the voluntary trust fund for the commission and the finance committee. we call upon other countries in a position to do so, to also contribute to these funds. now let me turn to the comments of the kingdom of the netherlands on the commission's report. the kingdom of the netherlands welcomes the work of the commission on assessing the performance of contractor activities, i would recall that my delegation proposed in 2000 2022 that the council request the commission to report on the names of the contractors that have repeatedly ignored calls from both the council as well as the commission to abide by their contractual obligation. as we noted then and we repeat here today, we believe that such a step is necessary in light of the prospect of the exploitation phase of deep sea mining coming closer. we need to set a compliance performance standard for exploration activities and institutionalize that practice as we approach the exploitation phase. therefore we are grateful to read that the commission is now applying the criteria contained in document, isba slash 29 slash ltc slash five for identifying contractors at risk of non compliance, with the aim of naming contractors that have responded inadequately or failed to respond. we know the council decision is by slash 29 slash c, slash 24 adopted in july 2024 where the council welcomed the development of these criteria in view of its continuing request that any such contractors be named in the annual report of the secretary general and agree to consider the ongoing implementation of the criteria at its next session, we look forward to hearing the annual report of the secretary general later this session, our second comment relates to the binding environmental threshold values. my delegation would like to express its sincere appreciation to the commission and the intersessional expert group on their continued work on developing the binding environmental threshold values. we note that the terms of reference for the intersessional expert group mentions that the work will focus on thresholds for poly metallic nodules, but is expected that thresholds will similarly be developed for cobalt rich ferro manganese crusts and poly metallic sulfide resources. these threshold values will form an indispensable part of the environmental protection regime as currently under development. we therefore, therefore, we would like to highlight that the kingdom of the netherlands, as expressed earlier in the council, wishes to see the development of binding environmental threshold values for other topics as well. in this regard, we welcome the fact that the report of the intersessional expert group is expected to identify scientific research needs and approaches for future review and development of the binding environmental threshold values. we are grateful to hear that the finalization of the draft report of the intersessional expert group will continue to be a priority for the commission, and we look forward to receiving its report. let me now touch upon a matter of particular importance to my delegation, that is the matter of regional environmental management plans. we wish to thank the commission for the extensive work on the development of the standardized procedure and template for the development, establishment and review of the regional environmental plan since the second part of the 29th session, we note with appreciation the efforts of the commission to incorporate all the comments received in this context. we also understand that the commission only address those comments that are of a scientific and or purely technical nature before deferring the other issues to council for consideration. we thank the commission for identifying three issues, and let me shortly comment on some of the points raised. first on the nature of the regional environmental management plans. my delegation notes that there are currently two ongoing discussions. one concerns the nature of standardized procedure and template used for the development, establishment and review of regional environmental management plans. the other second discussion concerns the nature of the regional environmental management plans adopted for a particular area and type of resource concerned. so the first discussion relates to the procedure by which the regional environmental management plan is established, and the second one relates to the outcome of that procedure. the kingdom of the netherlands has proposed to discuss and take up the discussion on the nature of the regional environmental management plans for a specific area in the new intersessional working group with respect to the nature of the standardized procedure and template, my delegation is of the opinion that column5: the president do thanks the ltc for its continued work and comprehensive report. do is encouraged to hear about the continued development of the environmental threshold values. the work of threshold working group is central to creating an effective environmental protection regime in developing thresholds, we note that is also important to consider the potential synergistic and or cumulative effects of impact, and the likelihood that these will lower individual thresholds. critically climate change effects on natural variability must also be considered as it will have multiple effects, including on sound propagation, species distribution, currents and water temperature and chemistry. further, there is a need for thresholds on acceptable levels of habitat loss, biodiversity loss and connectivity. without these thresholds, contractors in the ltc, ltc will not know whether states are willing to accept biodiversity loss as an impact from seabed mining. present levels of scientific knowledge tells us that deep seabed mining will result in biodiversity loss. that is a certainty given states obligations under unclos and the convention on biological diversity, it's therefore important to have threshold limits on biodiversity factors. we welcome the ltc view in para 22 that there is a need to adopt an evolutionary approach in the development and review of threshold values, including adaptive management measures, and that the intersessional expert group report is expected to identify scientific research needs and approaches for future review and development of thresholds. this seems to us a sensible approach. while developing the thresholds, we highlight. our understanding of this approach is that where there are significant uncertainties, the thresholds must be set at stringent and precautions levels and can be reviewed as knowledge increases over time. dos would like to reiterate that bad thresholds would be a worse situation than no thresholds at all. we thus want to emphasize how crucial it is that the thresholds are fit for purpose from the moment that they are implemented. in other words, thresholds cannot be implemented that pose uncertainties, with a view to them only reaching an adequate standard in the future, although they will, of course, continue to develop as scientific research develops. on paragraph 24 we look forward to the publication of the draft report of the intersessional expert group. this should include publication or all information on which the draft report is based, so that the underlying data and the report can be reviewed by scientists to inform the comments they provide during the consultation process. further, we want to stress the importance of holding a transparent and inclusive process and express our support for the ltc holding meetings in open session which would enhance the ability to assess how important scientific standards are being developed. on para 28 ac is encouraged to hear that there is support for the remps to follow a standardized procedure and for remps to be legally binding, as with the environmental objectives the standards and information is a plan to improve data, as this is very necessary. as a reminder, this should be done in a way that the data are implemented, implemented according to the fair principles, which is a global standard. the scientific community follows fair stands for findability accessibility interrupt interoperability and reuse. thank you mr. president. thank you,

recovery recovery permits under the eu us deep seabed, hard mineral resources, act of 1980 while this announcement does not does not in any way constitute an official notification, i must express my deep concern. it is imperative to reaffirm the authorities exclusive mandate. the authority remains the sole organization through which state parties show in accordance with part 11 of the united nations convention on the law of the sea and the 1994 agreement organize and control activities in the area, particularly in administering its resources. the area and its resources are proclaimed the common heritage of humankind under the convention, which serves as the constitution of the ocean. oceans all exploration and exploitation activities in the area must be carried out under the authorities control. this remains the only universally recognized legitimate framework any unilateral action would constitute a violation of international law and directly undermine the fundamental principles of multilateralism, the peaceful use of the oceans and the collective governance framework established under unclos for over three decades, the absence of claims under any regime outside part 11 has demonstrated the international community's strong confidence, including that of states, not party of the convention, and the system developed through the authority the principle of the common heritage of humankind as applied to the area, is a cornerstone of general international law and the fundamental pillar of ocean governance, widely upheld by the international community. our collective commitment to the rule of law and multilateral cooperation is essential of safeguarding this principle, i remain firmly dedicated to the authorities mandate ensuring that activities in the area are conducted for the benefit of all humankind. i take note with appreciation of the significant efforts of all council members during the session and their continued commitment to advancing negotiations of the draft exploitation regulations efficiently and in good faith. i reaffirm the secretary secretariat's full commitment to supporting the authorities member states in the critical steps ahead. the secretariat stands ready to assist the council in its intention to continue with the elaboration of rules, regulations and procedures relating to exploitation in accordance with the under water cultural heritage, just in draft regulation 35 or 35 alt or take a broader approach to the issue. the participants who spoke on the question generally supported a broader approach to underwater cultural heritage, although a number of those participants focused their comments on thursday on draft regulation 35 and 35 alt the second question asked participants to indicate their preference for either draft regulation 35 alt or 35 as well as their comments for the text of vulnerable regulations. most participants who spoke generally prefer draft regulation 35 alt to 35 although there was mention of support for draft regulation 35 that's a reasonable compromise between the various interests at stake. participants also express views on whether the commission or the council should be tasked with various roles under draft regulation 35 or 35 alt whether to go with one or the other approaches to consultations in paragraph four or four alt and whether to compensate contractors who are impacted under the draft regulation, among other issues. the third question asked participants who support a broad approach to underwater cultural heritage to indicate what their views were on the purpose and substance of those other draft regulations, the participants who responded referred to on the water cultural heritage in, for example, environmental impact statements and the overall environmental impact process in emmp, in underwater cultural heritage management plans and baseline surveys of the seabed participants also highlighted the relevance of the 2001 2003 unesco conventions on underwater cultural heritage and intangible cultural heritage, respectively. although there was a comment that while the work done by unesco would be covered by unclos, in a sense, there is a question as to whether the authority as a specific entity is allowed under the convention to address on the water cultural heritage via the mining code. participants additionally discussed whether there should be a standalone committee on the water cultural heritage, those who spoke generally supported its creation, although i again stress that the discussion ran out of time before we could hear from all interested members of the authority on this and other issues. there were also issues or views expressed about the long standing cultural connections of various indigenous peoples and local communities to the ocean, including the deep sea and seabed. the point was made about the need for a reciprocal relationship between humankind and the deep sea seabed, as well as the notion of proper stewardship of the marine environment. a point was made about how pure, intangible, underwater cultural heritage, such as some of the examples expressed in the discussion, might not particular cultural interest, there was also a bit of discussion on the issue of rights of indigenous peoples and of local communities, including their right to be consulted and involved in activities affecting them and their interests, with different and differing views expressed on the matter looking forward, my delegation believes that further work on underwater cultural heritage can and should acceptance of the need to reflect these matters in some form and the regulations. there has also been genuine and respectful engagement on the matter for multiple corners for which i remain deeply grateful. i have also taken note of the proposed additional modality of work for the council going forward in the form of friends of the president, i recommend that this new modality, if implemented, column5: thank you, mr. vice president, for giving me the floor. we are intervening on behalf of oceans north dscc and greenpeace international. we wish to thank the ltc for their hard work and for offering this opportunity to participate and comment in this intervention, we will address a number of matters, but note that we align with the environmental concerns to be raised in wwf international intervention. we are raising concerns regarding section e of the ltc report, with respect to the transparency of the ltc process of recommending an eis to the secretary general, we suggest that the process outlined in the report is not in line with the consultation recommendations within the exploration mining code. further concerns about the way these eia were conducted are detailed in stakeholder letters to the isa. but in particular, it is unclear how recommendation 60 7c and recommendation 68 from annex one of the recommendations were completed as they are not apparent in one of the october 2024 submissions from a contractor recommendation, recommendation 60 7c requires a description of the comments and concerns of the stakeholders and how they have been addressed by the contractor. in the environmental impact statement, only one of these eiss provide provided a response to the comment summaries, but the descriptions are minimal, and there was no opportunity provided for stakeholder response, this recommendation is especially important to ensure that stakeholders understand how and why their comments were integrated or not into this impact statement, and to provide an opportunity for the stakeholders to provide clarity or feedback in impact assessment best practice, stakeholders have multiple opportunities to view and take part in the evolution of the eis, thereby gaining an understanding of the outcome, considering the significant concerns of stakeholders in this process, transparency should be a primary value applied to the impact assessment process, especially as we move towards the evaluation of exploitation level impact assessments. a central registry for eia is essential to the values of transparency and participation. we also suggest that the consultation practices suggested in the exploration recommendations become consistent with best practice. these same principles apply more broadly to the ltc as a body, the council and its observers have on numerous occasions requested that the ltc meetings be open, which is still not the case. it is crucial that the ltc operate with the values of transparency and accountability. decisions and recommendations are being made for the benefit of human kind, and the recommendations from the ltc are extremely difficult for the council to reconsider and counteract, which means there are occasions where the ultimate decision power is not with the council members, but with a body that operates behind closed doors. we further note that in the ltc report, the call for increased support member states to ensure members are provided with the resources to engage with the ltc properly. with this in mind, we wish to understand the steps the ltc is considering to ensure further transparency and accountability in not just the eia processes, but. all process processes for which the ltc is responsible. lastly, we wish to echo france and belgium's concern regarding the renewal or extension of exploration contracts of a contractor identified in section f of the ltc report that is owned by a company seeking to conduct seabed mining activities in the area outside of the framework of unclos and would recommend that the members of the council and assembly give due consideration to their obligations under articles 137 to 139 of the convention to respond. thank you. i

column5: thank you for the floor. mister president, distinguished delegates, members of the council as an observer to the international seabed authority. the international telecommunication union is pleased to contribute to the council's deliberations on matters within its mandate, particularly those related to telecommunications submarine infrastructure. in november 2024 the itu, in partnership with the international cable protection committee, icpc, launched the international advisory body for submarine cable resilience, which aims to enhance resilience of the global submarine cable network by pooling technical expertise, best practices and collaboration across different stakeholders. the advisory body co chaired by his excellency minister, boson tujani, minister of communications, innovation and digital economy, the federal republic of nigeria and professor sandra maximiano, chair of anacom. board of directors portugal includes 42 members from both the public and private sectors. these include representatives from submarine cable operators, telecommunications companies, equipment suppliers as well as service providers, government agencies responsible for digital infrastructure and international organizations, it specifically addresses issues such as improving cable maintenance, preventing damage from natural hazards and human activities, ensuring faster recovery times after disruptions, increase redundancy and promoting sustainable practices in the industry. in addition, it works to help strengthen cooperation between countries and companies to protect this vital infrastructure that underpins global communications and digital economy. five intergovernmental organizations have a consultative role within the body, fao, imo, un id, ir, un du wallos and un oc. an invitation was sent to isa last year, and a new one recently said to the isa new secretary general on 26 to 27th of february, 2025 the international submarine cable resilience summit was held in abuja, nigeria, bringing together the global community to address critical technical issues related to submarine cable resilience. it also marked the first in person gathering of the advisory body members. the event provided a platform to deepen dialog and generate actionable strategies to ensure the resilience of submarine cable systems worldwide. the resulting summit declaration outlines collective commitments to safeguarding submarine cable systems and ensuring global connectivity. during may 2025 three working groups were established by the advisory body to focus on key areas that are critical to the strengthening global submarine cable resilience working group, one timely deployment and repair co facilitated by mister zhou, the chief engineer of the ministry of industry and information technology of the people's republic of china, mister kevin adams, deputy director for telecom security and resilience, department of science innovation and technology, united kingdom, working group two with risk, risk reduction, risk identification, monitoring and mitigation, co facilitated by miss nong pela tatekale jordan diani, director general of the department of communications and digital technologies of south africa, mister andy palmer felgate, acting president of north american submarine cable association and working group three fostering connectivity and geographic diversity. co facilitated by mister sanbu kim, vice president of digital of the world bank and yours truly, rodney taylor, secretary general of the caribbean telecommunications union. these working groups, with a total of more than 160 expert members nominated by governments, industry and academia and international organizations, represent a diverse cross section of global stakeholders. each working group is co led by two appointed facilitators, as i pointed out, and it starts with producing an action oriented report or other deliverables by early 2025 these reports will include concrete recommendations and best practices aimed at enhancing resilience of submarine cable infrastructure worldwide, given the isa mandate to ensure the effective protection of the marine environment from harmful effects that may arise from deep seabed related activities and the role it may play to improve the protection of under sea infrastructure. the itu wishes to highlight this matter and is willing to engage further with the isa to explore potential areas of collaboration. thank you very much, mister president.

column4: general reflections; "we are not divided by land, but connected by ocean"; acknowledges that isa has been seen as intransparent and opaque, even dysfunctional and corrupt; asks for time to turn the ship around; says personal attacks on her or the team is an attack on the isa; says attacks are intended to sow doubts, to destabilise; asks what the council intends to do going forward; [i assume this statement gets published on the website]
column5: thank you, mr. president and isa council members for the opportunity to remark on the progress by the finance committee, notably on benefit sharing through the proposed common heritage fund. should this be agreed by this esteemed body, we will be one step closer to the aspirations of equity and the fair sharing of resources from areas deemed as civilizations, global commons laid out by the visionary avid pado in 19 767, that lie at the heart of the international seabed authorities mandate successful, successful achievement of this aspiration is our has on death row, consequently, having a tangible pathway to turn ambition to realization is a moment we can all be proud of showing our true collective commitment, our ability to make real progress despite the intricacies of our mission. with this, i respectfully encourage council members to act on this recommendation of the finance committee to set us on the course to a pioneering accomplishment for the good of all humanity. and now, as we come to the end of our second week of council, my second as secretary general, please indulge me a few moments to reflect. i'm sure we can all agree that the fact that our principles are so deeply embedded in equity and fairness, inclusive of all geographies, from land to sea, make the mandate of this organization highly complex, and it can be polarizing, frustrating, it can even be hostile. but in this mandate, regardless of our various positions, we are not divided by land, but connected by ocean, whether we represent a landlocked nation, a coastal country or a big ocean state, whether we are ready, we are already a developed nation or on the path to becoming we are in this together, dedicated to ensuring that we do things better and to avoid mistakes on the past, done on the past. as a person who has spent my entire career in public service, i deeply believe in this mission, but the road for pioneers is not easy. it is full of crossroads and chaos. i was fully aware of the challenges that would face, that i would face in leading this institution. it is no secret that we have been viewed as slow and opaque and portrayed as everything from dysfunctional to corrupt. however, i was fully confident and committed that guiding the isa towards the fit for purpose vision that the isa family entrusted me with, guiding the isa towards greater transparency, inclusivity, accountability, and, crucially, effectiveness. but change is never easy. it takes time, and there is inevitably a phase that fuels messy, as i said, when this body overwhelmingly elected me, my first steps, starting six months ago, when i took leadership, were to listen, learn and adapt the processes and practices, both externally and internally, to achieve organizational excellence, to put us on a path to reach the collective vision, noting, in this sense, i note and i reaffirm nothing has changed. i therefore, humbly request you grant me the time needed to get the house in order and to remember that personal attacks on me, on my team, are attacks on this institution attempt to disrupt our important work, to flood the zone with endless defamation, to sue seeds of doubt, to essentially make the isa appear as destabilized. destabilizing forces want us to appear, veering us away from integrity and purpose as promised. from the beginning of my tenure, my door is always open to hear and address any concerns you have, and for your guidance and wisdom on making the isa into the organization we need for the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead. there will be mistakes made, but i submit to you that one of the most important aspects of achieving this vision is to keep working hard. keep working hard, improving our processes and modalities of work, setting ambitions but attainable milestones, staying focused and adopting crucial mandates such as the periodic review that will create a platform to optimize transparency and accountability. just as markets need clarity and benchmarks from which to measure, so do great institutions, as we had to assembly. i very much look forward to hearing from council on what success will look like for the end of this meeting, and how you envision a vision steering the course for the intersessional period. on behalf of the isa secretariat, i and my team stand at your service to deliver on your guidance and ambition. in closing, on monday, we celebrate le cator juliet. its mantra is liberty, equality, fraternity. tomorrow, marks nelson mandela day, honoring the life and legacy of a man who was the very embodiment of rising above difference, to embrace all to achieve a vision of humanity at its finest. i take the opportunity to congratulate our council members, friends and south africa on these observances, and to ask us all to embrace their symbolism and teams of ubuntu togetherness to keep progressing on our noble mission. i really thank you, president for allowing me the time and the council members for listening.

column4: thanks everyone; concerned about non-payment by members; asks for the un to do audits and not an external audit company; hard critique of the way the financial benefit sharing mechanism is being develop; wants council or assembly involved; critiques that only a fund is being considered and not other options; fiery statement
column5: costa rica, thanks the finance committee for the full report presented and for the important work carried out by its members. we know that these are busy people who are moreover working for free, and they do conscientious work, which is why we congratulate them and thank them. moreover, i'm delighted to see my old friend ken at the head of this important organ subsidiary to the assembly, which is a guarantee that the body will function very well. welcome back. we also thank madam secretary general for her words. madam secretary general, costa rica believes in your commitment to accountability, transparency and strengthening the governance of the authority, and you can count on our full support. today is also the day for international law. so it's a honor to spend this in this day, in this organization, which is also working towards international justice, or one aspect thereof, costa rica, moving now to the report expresses its concern for the contributions that have not yet been paid. we know that all countries are in a difficult fiscal situation, but we are concerned particularly by the 43 delegations that are at least two years in arrears. and we are urging the secretariat to continue to communicate with these countries and to study potential payment agreements that allow these states to fulfill their obligations. costa rica also takes notes of the selection of the same audit company for the upcoming period, and and we consider that if the committee has approved this new contract, the authority should move forward. and costa rica supports this decision. but we need to keep in mind that this committee, since 2009 has asked to request the un to do the audit. they have been requesting it since 2009 and since then, costa rica, every year was saying, well, why don't we respect what the finance committee has told us to do? we never received a response. there was no follow up to this request, but my delegation consider that this would be the right moment to insist on this recommendation, since we are at the beginning of a new administration, administration given the status for the participation of the members of the ltc and the finance committee, costa rica is somewhat concerned that there is a lack of funds, and it is urging those that have generously contributed in the past to continue to support those funds with the funds necessary, so that the representatives of developing countries could take part in all of those meetings. i will now focus on the main topic, i would say, at the hands of the finance committee, which is to say, to develop a proposal for the mechanism for benefit sharing. point 11 of the report, we thank you for the information share on the development of rules for a fair share of the benefits. the benefits is one of the most important elements of the legal framework to adopt before we begin mining activities, since this is the common heritage of humankind, we need to make sure, through this process that the major benefit be for humankind, as indicates article 140 of unclos and the responsibility of the council, according to article 160 2.2 is to recommend to the assembly the standards, rules, regulations, procedures for the fed, equitable distribution of benefits, and it's then an obligation of the assembly to adopt them according to article 160 the there are many topics that we have not discussed. for example, in article 140 we speak of financial benefits and other economic benefits, and there is no distinction made between financial benefits on the one hand and other benefits on the other hand. we don't know if the intention refers to the provisions on the transfer of technology, which, before the 1994 agreement, had a more defined aspect. moreover, there might be other economic benefits for seeing such as consumers that been that would benefit from lower prices of metals. there the authority has no mechanism to redistribute these benefits, and due to these limitations the debate, we could argument. we could say that article 140 is based on the revenue that will the mining proceeds that are coming to the authority. but this topic, and many other topics have not been discussed by us, which is why costa rica reiterates the importance that this topic, which is an individual topic, that we be presented to the council and the assembly. we believe that this needs to be a specific point on the agenda. we are concerned, and we have indicated this over the last two years, that without this having been distributed by the council or the assembly, the finance committee is focused on developing the option of a common fund as the mechanism to to gather the proceeds of mining. three years ago, when the delegation started asking questions on the amounts that the states would receive based on the royalties that were being computed or that were being proposed by the financial mechanism? the previous secretary general suggested that, instead of preparing a model for the benefit sharing amongst countries, we created a single fund, many delegations did not agree in focusing the work exclusively on that option, even though we agreed that this should be one of the options to be under study, this decision of a common fund, instead of an economic distribution to the states can only be taken by the states themselves, and before that, no option should be rejected. and this is what my delegation has requested with others since 2023 for costa rica, it is very important that we have a real assessment on the economic benefits that will be shared individually with the states party. we need to know how much each state would receive depending on the system of royalties that will be adopted. this will help us to make a decision on the royalties. there is a projection made by the african group, which always brings to bear important contributions, where it was estimated that what was would be received by countries would be less than $100,000 and this is without taking into account well, this with the royalties that were being foreseen, and this without taking into account that first we need to cover the administrative costs of the authority and then pay the land the countries with land based mining. so it is necessary to develop a benefit sharing model which allows us to know at least more or less how much would be the economic benefits with royalties at 10% 15% 20% and this would help us to decide what we want to aim for and what amount we will consider necessary in order to justify that we are consuming the heritage of humankind, and we need to to to decide how we will do the distribution. will it be per capita? will we develop a multi dimensional index, possibly for all countries, or would it be different percentages for less developed countries or developing countries? will the states that are non parties to unclos have rights, and under which conditions should they and should they fulfill their obligations since 1994 and pay their dues? these are many issues that we have never discussed and that costa rica. costa rica considers that should be studied within the council and within the assembly. costa rica is concerned that the development of the only this option of the general fund does not allow us to fully understand the various options before us, and we believe that a subsidiary organ which has as a function to make recommendations and to whom we have requested to continue to study all the options should so do. this was clear in document isba, 20, 8c, 11, add one, the statement of the president to the council section three in section f of the report of the finance committee, where it is mentioned that many country requested that we continue to study the various options in the same page, web page of the authority, if you look for benefit sharing, it is said, this is precisely said, and invited the finance committee to continue working on both the equitable distribution formula and on the common heritage fund for the equitable sharing sigue embargo solo simple caron en el fondo. however, they seem to have only focused on the fund. and it may be mr. president and madam secretary general that the states decide that the best option is the fund, but we would only be able to decide that after having analyzed the different options available to us. for that reason, costa rica cannot support the recommendations of the ltc recommendation d because it is limited only to using the fund as the only mechanism for the fair distribution of benefits, where we're in agreement that we should move forward on this analysis, but together with other options, other models, and that's why we are again requesting that this be included in the next agenda, in the agenda of the next meeting of council and of the assembly, not as part of a report from the committee, from the finance committee, but as an independent issue, because of the importance that it has for us that we be able to analyze and be able to come to an agreement, we respectfully request to the president to include this request in the report. thank you, mr. president.

column5: thank you, mr. president, for giving me the floor. sierra leone takes the floor on behalf of the african group. the african group. thanks the secretary general for remarks, especially on the concept of ubuntu. at the outset, the african group commence the work of the finance committee, particularly the leadership of the committee's chair. the african group has consistently prioritized the work of the finance committee as a key organ of the authority responsible for supporting the implementation of its mandates, which currently focuses on developing regulations for the exploitation of mineral resources in the area. mr. president on the report from the chair of the finance committee the african group would like to make the following comments. one we express concern regarding paragraph eight, where the committee discussed paragraph 19 of the finance committee report from the 29th session isba, slash 29 slash a, slash nine is 29 slash c, slash 20 about the reclassification of posts within the secretariat. we also acknowledge the committee's position of not endorsing the elements in document, isba slash 30, slash a slash seven, concerning the structuring of the secretariat, mr. president, this issue of is of significant concern to the african group, given the assembly decision is bas slash 29 slash a, slash three, add one, east bas slash 29 slash c, slash 11, at one paragraph 19, which explicitly stated that no classification decision should be carried out without prior approval from the assembly, based on the recommendation of the finance committee. it should be noted that the previous restructuring was carried out following a review under article 154, the african group will therefore require a report from the secretary general explaining the reasons behind the recent reclassification of posts within the secretariat, including why the reclassification was done without prior approval from the assembly, as required, the legal and financial implications of the decision and its effect on the affected staff members. in this regard, we support the committee's request for the secretariat to provide an update on staffing tables, including a breakdown of staff and consultants for the council's consideration, mister president. we further note in paragraph nine of the port matters related to ongoing litigation before the joint appeals board and the united nations appeals tribunal, and wish to express concern about these litigations which could have financial implications for the authority, without prejudice to the confidentiality of the cases. we also urge the secretary general to provide an update on the issues before the tribunal and an overview of the potential financial implications of these cases, the issues mentioned above are severe and need careful thoughts. the african group family believes in the crucial role that authority plays in protecting the common heritage of humankind and ensuring that the benefits of the ocean are preserved for everyone. achieving this critical goal relies on the dedication and commitment of the authority staff, therefore the treatment and well being of the staff must be given the highest priority. a motivated and dedicated team is vital for the authorities productivity the authority staff should be able to depend on a stable, predictable and reliable working conditions. wish to bring the council's attention to the issues highlighted in the report of the finance committee, and strongly encourage the secretary general to prepare a report, as requested, mister president, on the audited financial statement of the authority for 2024 the african group commence the auditor's opinion that the financial statements present, present an accurate and fair view of the authorities financial position as of december 31 2024 and its financial performance and cash flows for the year then ended. it is also encouraging to note that the auditor had no adverse comments. we also commend the secretariat for its careful management of the finances of the authority during the period under review. mister president regarding the updated financial status of the authorities partnership fund as of may 3120 25 it has a balance of $1,025,679 and the trust fund for extra budget is support stands at 567,660 $9,000 however, it is concerning that both the voluntary trust fund for participation of members of the legal and technical commission and the finance committee from developing countries, as well as the voluntary trust fund to support the participation of members of the council from developing states have a negative balance after providing financial support to these members for their participation in the meetings of the second part of the 30th session of the authority, the african group notes the critical role of the voluntary trust funds in supporting the participation of members and representatives from developing countries in the work of the authority. the african group joins the committee and expressing its appreciation to the donors who have made contributions to the voluntary trust funds of the authority. it also encourages members, observers, contractors and other stakeholders to contribute financially to the trust funds. given the current financial situation, it is noted with appreciation that the finance committee has taken action on the common heritage fund by recommending it to the council and assembly, we encourage the committee to explore alternative models for distributing income from activities in the area, and recommend to the council all options for consideration we equally support the call on the secretariat to develop the concept of the fund as the way for distributing income from activities in the area to be shared. according to articles, 140 and article 160 sub article two, paragraph g, as prescribed in article 173 of the convention. we note with appreciation, part four of this report, which addresses the status of contributions and related matters, the african group, emphasizes that the continuous implementation of unclos is a noble and collective responsibility, one that demands an all hands on deck approach from member states and all recognized actors under the convention, it is understood that contributions are essential for the effective functioning of the authorities activities. in this regard, we respectfully urge member states with outstanding contributions to settle their years as we emphasize the importance of solidarity and shared commitment to the authorities aims. furthermore, we align ourselves with the committee's commendation of the secretary general's diligent follow up in efforts to address unpaid contributions. these efforts, which include regular notices, bilateral engagements and awareness raising initiatives, are pivotal in fostering the culture of timely compliance and financial responsibility. in conclusion, mr. president the african group wishes to thank the chair of the finance committee for his leadership, as well as all committee members for their hard work, and assures its intention to engage constructively. finally, we express our support for the recommendations of the finance committee.

column5: mr. president. we are grateful to the chair of the finance committee for presenting the committee's report, and we thank all members of the committee for their work. we also thank the secretary general for her remarks, and wish to assure her of our support, particularly in her reform agenda. we also welcome her commitment to transparency and her willingness to engage with members of the authority on issues of concern. we note that delegations have sought clarifications in respect of certain matters, and we are confident that these will be addressed in the same spirit of collegiality and transparency. on the question of reform, we wish to speak to one particular issue, namely the existing auditing arrangements. we wish to express our support to the remarks of costa rica on this matter. if we are an organization committed to even basic standards of good governance, then it is absolutely imperative that we transition to more rigorous auditing procedures. ireland fully supports calls for the authority to avail of the un auditing system as a matter of priority. if there is a cost involved in this, we need to be prepared to pay it. the authority is taking on ever more responsibilities, and in the near future, is likely to be handling very significant financial sums. with this comes the need for better oversight and safeguards.

in document ispa 38 a eight and is bar 30 c 12, as a small island developing state and a sponsoring state committed to responsible governance of the area. the kingdom of tonga supports the continued efforts of the authority to uphold sound financial management, institutional transparency and equitable participation in its work. the kingdom of tonga takes note of the prudent execution of the 2023 and 2020 and 2024 budget and commends the secretariat for managing expenditure within approved limits, despite operational pressures and market related challenges. encourage ongoing efforts to column5: we would like to start by thanking the finance committee for their work. we have two issues first to raise, with regards to stuffing matters. first is on the restructuring issues. we note that recent restructuring of the secretariat has been accomplished within the approved budget for the period of 2025 to 2026 however, we echo the concerns of african group on this issue in the decision of the assembly last year on the budget of the authority that is isba, slash 29 slash a slash 11, the assembly requested the secretary general to implement recommendations of the finance committee without delay, including providing explicit administrative instruction that no reclassification decision would be implemented without prior approval of the assembly on the recommendation of the finance committee. it is therefore strange to us that your recent restructuring of the secretariat was conducted without regard to the decision of the assembly. furthermore, we note that an administrative instruction that is isba, slash st slash ai slash 2023, slash three, slash amend two was published in january 2025 amending the procedures for classification and reclassification of posts so that the secretary general may directly authorize the reclassification of a position as a result of restructuring without requiring prior submission to standard classification procedures. this amendment was authorized by the secretary general. we consider that this clearly goes against the decision of the assembly that no reclassification decision would be implemented without prior approval of the assembly on the recommendation of the finance committee. we are also concerned that the finance committee was unable to reach a conclusion on the legal framework and conditioning and condition of the recent restructuring of the secretariat. in this regard, we respectfully request two things, first, given that this amendment of the procedures for classification and reclassification of posts is not in line with the decision of the assembly. we request confirmation from the secretariat that the decision of the assembly in isba, slash 29 slash a slash 11 will be fully respected and implemented over what is set out in the amendment. second, we request for the finance committee to share their considerations in assessing the legal framework and condition of the recent restructuring of the secretariat. we also agree and reiterate the finance committee's recommendation that in the future, no reclassification decision should be implemented without prior approval of the assembly, on the recommendation of the finance committee. second on the ongoing litigation between the joint appeals board and the un abuse tribunal, we note that at the request of the finance committee, the secretariat provided an update on this matter, including an overview of potential financial scenarios. without prejudice to the confidentiality of these cases, we request for the potential financial scenarios to be shared with member states for info, for information, including potential legal costs and financial liabilities that the authority may incur in the event of unfavorable decisions. we also request for the finance committee to be regularly informed of the legal processes so that they can assess financial liabilities for the authority. we further note that the joint abuse board was dismantled temporarily without explanation, which coincided with complaints from former staff members on unfair hr actions. such structures are put in place to ensure the integrity of the authority. this is important for the isa, which is a principled, transparent and rules based organization. moving on to other parts of the report, we appreciate the secretary general's efforts to follow up on unpaid contributions, and we encourage member states in a res to make their contributions as soon as possible. we also agree with the proposed changes to annual overhead charges to align with actual costs incurred. and we also agree with the finance committee's recommendation that the secretariat develop the concept of the common heritage fund via a comprehensive report.
